purpose: Butenafine is used to treat fungal skin infections like athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It helps clear up the rash, itching, and irritation caused by these infections. It is applied directly to the skin and is available over the counter or by prescription.
how_it_works: Butenafine works by blocking the fungus from making an important substance it needs to build its outer wall. Without this substance, the fungal cells break down and die. This stops the infection from spreading and helps your skin heal.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medicine very well. Some people may notice mild burning, stinging, redness, or itching right where they apply it. These reactions are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use butenafine in your eyes, mouth, or vagina — it is only meant for the skin. If you develop severe irritation, blistering, or an allergic reaction such as rash or swelling, stop using it and contact your doctor. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medication. Do not stop using it early even if your skin looks better — finishing the full course helps prevent the infection from coming back.
typical_dosing: For athlete's foot between the toes, apply it once a day for 4 weeks, or twice a day for 1 week. For jock itch or ringworm, apply it once a day for 2 weeks. Always apply a thin layer to the affected area and a little of the skin around it. Wash your hands after applying.
